question: What is the correct evaluation protocol for 'transfer to deeper multi-hop queries' — is there an established held-out-hop split (e.g. train 1-2 hop, test 3 hop) on MetaQA/WebQSP/CWQ, or must a new hop-controlled split be constructed, and does the field report it?
description: MetaQA is naturally stratified by hop count (1/2/3-hop), which suggests a natural transfer protocol; WebQSP/CWQ are ~2-hop. Whether prior work reports train-on-shallow/test-on-deep transfer determines if the central claim is comparable to existing numbers or needs a bespoke setup.
confidence_basis: Based on the 9 analyzed papers and abstracts; no dedicated search for hop-generalization protocols was run, so absence of evidence is not strong evidence of absence.
rationale: If no established hop-transfer protocol exists, the headline finding has no baseline to compare against and the evaluation must be designed from scratch, changing the contribution substantially.
resolution: Partially resolved: MetaQA is naturally hop-stratified (1/2/3-hop) and NSM reports separate results per hop level, but no retrieved work reports an explicit train-on-shallow/test-on-deeper-hop transfer protocol as a headline result. So the idea's central transfer claim currently has no directly comparable published baseline and would need a bespoke, pre-registered split. A targeted search for length/hop generalization protocols in KGQA and multi-hop reasoning is still needed.
